reason: The passage explicitly depicts Yahweh as having a covenant relationship with the nation of Israel. God identifies himself as 'the God of your fathers' (linking to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob), states that 'the cry of the children of Israel has come to me,' affirms that He has 'seen the oppression which Egypt is oppressing them,' and commands Moses to bring out 'my people, the children of Israel' from Egypt. Throughout the passage, the Israelites are referred to as Yahweh's people (עַמִּי), and God establishes a special, particularistic relationship with this nation. This is the defining characteristic of a national deity in ancient Near Eastern religious contexts.
